analysis.title: High Frequency Monitor: Sentiment vs earnings
key_insights: Global equities fell -0.3% last week on concerns about monetization of AI capex and the inflationary impact of the persistent Middle East conflict. Global equities are down -3.3% over eight weeks.
Despite negative sentiment, 82.7% of US companies have surprised on the upside in the current earnings season. The Earnings Revision Ratio (ERR) remains high for Developed Markets at 1.19.
Best global sectors last week: Health Care (+3.0%), Insurance (+1.6%), Real Estate (+1.5%). Worst: Media & Ent. (-8.5%), Software (-3.0%), Semiconductors (-1.0%).
Best global themes last week: Nuclear Energy (+3.0%), Rare Earths (+2.4%), Precision Medicine (+2.3%). Worst: SaaS (-4.9%), Cybersecurity (-4.2%), Quantum Computing (-3.5%).

YTD the best themes are AI Compute (+58%), Photonics (+56%) and Data Centers (+30%). Nuclear Energy is the worst YTD at -18%. AI Compute (-17.9%), Photonics (-21.6%) and Data Centers (-16.8%) are down sharply over the last month.

Triple Momentum (earnings, price, news) is strongest for global Tech Hardware, Semiconductors and Energy. Top-ranked large liquid names include Kioxia, Montage Tech-A, Zhongji Innolight-A, Neste, Renesas, SEMCO, Murata, Panasonic, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust and Elite Material.

Regional last-week returns (USD): Europe +1.3%, Asia Pac ex-Japan +0.6%, Global -0.3%, Japan -0.6%, USA -0.7%. MTD: Europe +0.3%, USA -1.0%, Global -4.2%, Japan -6.9%, APxJ -8.1%. YTD: Japan +15.6%, APxJ +13.3%, GEM +11.6%, USA +10.5%, Global +9.9%, Europe +4.1%.

MTD sector leaders are Energy (+11.6%), Cons. Staples (+9.9%) and Health Care (+9.2%). Laggards are Media & Ent. (-14.7%), Semiconductors (-13.3%) and Tech Hardware (-5.4%). YTD Energy is +45.7%, Tech Hardware +35.2%, Semiconductors +34.1%, Media & Ent. -14.6%.

Breadth is narrow: the ACWI returned 10.0% over 12 months against 3.3% for the equal-weighted index, and only 37% of stocks outperformed the index over 12 months (34% YTD). Last week 57% outperformed.

Style: Growth led last week (+3.2% relative), Value (-0.7%) and Momentum (-1.3%) lagged. MTD Quality (+5.9%) and Dividend (+5.1%) lead while Momentum (-9.8%) and Risk (-8.8%) lag. YTD Dividend (+12.7%) leads.

The Global Wave troughed in Feb-26 and gives a positive signal. Global prospective EPS has improved 38% in the last 12 months. The Global Wave has a 0.75 correlation with the YoY change in prospective EPS.
The global ERR fell to 0.94 in Nov wk2 from 1.01, with the trend moderating. Regional ERR: Japan 2.06, Europe 1.06, USA 1.05, World 0.94, EM 0.71, APxJ 0.71. Taiwan is strongest in Asia at 2.08.
Sector ERR is strongest in Energy (2.00), Tech Hardware (1.75) and Banks (1.52), and weakest in Cons. Discretionary (0.56). Momentum style ERR rose to 2.79 and Growth is 1.93.

The Global News Pulse improved last week but fell month to date. Japan has the strongest regional pulse (63%) and Europe the weakest (33%). Energy has the strongest sector pulse (73%). Taiwan and Thailand lead the country pulses. Top news mentions were Apple, Alphabet, Meta, SpaceX Starship, Google Gemini and Apple Pay.
The most recent Market Trough Monitor signal was 01-Oct-24. Historically ACWI has averaged 28% (27.0% in the table) in the 12 months after a trough signal, with a 100% hit rate at 1 year.
The VIX moved from 19.5 to 19.4 and V2X from 21.9 to 22.1. VKOSPI is 52.3, VNKY fell from 38.3 to 33.8 and VXEEM rose from 29.2 to 31.0.

Markets price 60 bps of Fed hikes over the next 12 months. The Fed balance sheet fell US$10bn last week. US 10-year yield fell 7 bps to 4.93% and the 90-day yield fell 5 bps to 4.08%. Global credit spreads widened 6 bps.
US initial jobless claims fell by 1,000 to 194,000.
Commodities last week: Natural Gas +9.8%, Silver -8.7%, Gold -2.7%, Copper -1.0%, Crude Oil +0.8%. Crude Oil is +17.8% MTD and +82.9% YTD. Silver is -18.6% MTD.

Valuation: global prospective PE is 16.6 and global price-to-book is 3.71 (30-Oct). The USA is the most expensive region (P/B 5.58, PE 19.2) and EM the cheapest on PE (8.4). At the current P/B, ACWI averaged 0% over the following 12 months, while at the current PE it averaged 9%.

Themes with top-quintile Triple Momentum are AI Compute, Data Centers, Photonics, Grid Modernisation and Cybersecurity. Nuclear Energy, Rare Earths, Alcoholic Beverages, Luxury Lifestyle and Consulting are in the bottom quintile.
Revenue-exposure YTD: APxJ-exposed US stocks outperformed by 24.7% and China-exposed by 14.1%. Mexico-exposed stocks underperformed by 11.0%.
